result.title: Dynamic Graph World Modelling: Learning Future Dynamics from Temporal Context
result.summary: Dynamic graph learning models how entities and their relations evolve from historical observations to predict future graph states. Existing methods do not fully address dynamic graph world modelling, which requires learning transitions from temporal context to future latent graph states. This is difficult for three reasons: nodes and relations rely on different historical evidence, structural evolution is path-dependent, and future snapshots provide sparse and realization-specific targets. We propose Dynamic Graph World Modelling (DyG-WM), the first framework to jointly predict future node and relation representations from temporal context by answering three questions: what has evolved, how it evolved, and what will evolve next. To capture what has evolved, a historical node-relation context encoder summarizes node-neighborhood trajectories and pair-specific histories. To characterize how it evolved, a node-relation path-signature encoder captures ordered structural changes. To predict what will evolve next, a dual-level joint-embedding objective predicts target-snapshot node and relation representations without reconstructing the raw graph. Experiments on 12 link-prediction and two node-classification datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of DyG-WM across both tasks.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 DyG-WM 框架，从历史时序上下文出发联合预测未来的节点与关系表示，分别用历史节点-关系上下文编码器、路径签名编码器和双层级联合嵌入目标刻画「已演变什么、如何演变、接下来演变什么」，在 12 个链接预测与 2 个节点分类数据集上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「不重建原始图、直接在隐空间预测未来状态」的联合嵌入目标，以及路径签名对有序结构变化的编码，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态预测任务、信息坍缩规避和深度/位置顺序编码提供可核查的方法线索。
